title: Airspace Pipeline Monitoring
description: Pipeline health, Kafka, Spark, Airflow, PostgreSQL and data quality for the OpenSky pipeline.

panels.title: Component status

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT *, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - sampled_at) AS age_s FROM pipeline_monitor_samples ORDER BY sampled_at DESC LIMIT 1
),
r AS (
  SELECT * FROM pipeline_airflow_runs WHERE dag_id = 'opensky_pipeline'
  ORDER BY COALESCE(started_at, queued_at) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 1 AS ord, 'Monitor' AS component,
       CASE WHEN age_s <= 180 THEN 'OK' ELSE 'DOWN' END AS status,
       'last sample ' || round(age_s)::int || ' s ago' AS detail FROM s
UNION ALL
SELECT 2, 'Kafka (aircraft_states)',
       CASE WHEN age_s > 180 THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN kafka_ok THEN 'OK' ELSE 'DOWN' END,
       CASE WHEN kafka_end_offset IS NULL THEN 'broker or topic not reachable' ELSE 'end offset ' || kafka_end_offset END FROM s
UNION ALL
SELECT 3, 'Ingestion',
       CASE WHEN age_s > 180 THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN ingestion_last_file_at IS NULL THEN 'DOWN'
            WHEN now() - ingestion_last_file_at <= interval '10 minutes' THEN 'OK' ELSE 'STALE' END,
       CASE WHEN ingestion_last_file_at IS NULL THEN 'no Parquet output found'
            ELSE 'last Parquet ' || round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - ingestion_last_file_at) / 60)::int || ' min ago' END FROM s
UNION ALL
SELECT 4, 'Spark streaming',
       CASE WHEN age_s > 180 THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN NOT spark_ok THEN 'DOWN'
            WHEN now() - spark_committed_at <= interval '10 minutes' THEN 'OK'
            WHEN ingestion_last_file_at IS NULL OR now() - ingestion_last_file_at > interval '10 minutes' THEN 'IDLE'
            ELSE 'STALLED' END,
       CASE WHEN spark_committed_at IS NULL THEN 'no committed batch'
            ELSE 'batch ' || spark_batch || ' committed ' || round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - spark_committed_at) / 60)::int || ' min ago' END FROM s
UNION ALL
SELECT 5, 'Airflow (opensky_pipeline)',
       CASE WHEN s.age_s > 180 OR NOT s.airflow_ok OR r.run_id IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN'
            WHEN r.state IN ('running', 'queued') AND now() - COALESCE(r.started_at, r.queued_at) > interval '30 minutes' THEN 'STUCK'
            WHEN r.state = 'running' THEN 'RUNNING' WHEN r.state = 'queued' THEN 'QUEUED'
            WHEN r.state = 'failed' THEN 'FAILED'
            WHEN now() - COALESCE(r.ended_at, r.started_at) > interval '2 hours' THEN 'STALE'
            ELSE 'OK' END,
       CASE WHEN NOT s.airflow_ok THEN 'Airflow metadata DB not readable'
            WHEN r.run_id IS NULL THEN 'no DAG run recorded'
            ELSE 'latest run ' || COALESCE(r.state, '?') || ', ' || round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - COALESCE(r.started_at, r.queued_at)) / 60)::int || ' min ago' END
FROM s LEFT JOIN r ON true
UNION ALL
SELECT 6, 'Data in PostgreSQL',
       CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN now() - m <= interval '15 minutes' THEN 'LIVE'
            WHEN now() - m <= interval '90 minutes' THEN 'RECENT' ELSE 'STALE' END,
       CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN 'no observations' ELSE 'newest observation ' || round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - m) / 60)::int || ' min old' END
FROM (SELECT max(observation_time) AS m FROM aircraft_observations) d
UNION ALL
SELECT 7, 'PostgreSQL', 'OK',
       'answering queries; ' || (SELECT numbackends FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database()) || ' connection(s)'
ORDER BY ord

panels.description: Inferred from the monitor's last sample, Airflow's run records and PostgreSQL. Container up/down is not collected (no Docker socket is mounted). UNKNOWN = the monitor sample is older than 3 minutes. Ingestion/Spark use the same 10-minute window as the Airflow checks; Spark is IDLE (not STALLED) when ingestion has produced nothing new either. Airflow is STUCK when a run has been queued/running for more than 30 minutes.

panels.title: Newest observation age

targets.rawSql: SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - max(observation_time)) / 60.0 AS "minutes" FROM aircraft_observations

panels.description: Same tiers as the Streamlit dashboard: up to 15 min = live window, up to 90 min = recent snapshot, older = stale. PostgreSQL is loaded hourly, so this is the age of the newest LOADED observation.

targets.rawSql: SELECT max(observation_time) AS "t" FROM aircraft_observations

panels.title: Last scheduled loader success

targets.rawSql: SELECT max(loader_ended_at) AS "t" FROM pipeline_airflow_runs WHERE dag_id = 'opensky_pipeline' AND run_type = 'scheduled' AND loader_state = 'success'

panels.description: postgres_loader task of the latest successful SCHEDULED opensky_pipeline run, from Airflow's metadata DB. Manual loader runs (docker compose run --rm loader) are not Airflow runs; see the next panel.

panels.title: Last load that added rows

targets.rawSql:
SELECT max(sampled_at) AS "t" FROM (
          SELECT sampled_at, pg_latest_observation, lag(pg_latest_observation) OVER (ORDER BY sampled_at) AS prev
          FROM pipeline_monitor_samples) x
        WHERE pg_latest_observation > prev

panels.description: Detected by the monitor as the moment the newest observation_time advanced (any loader run, manual or Airflow). Only covers the time since the monitor was started; a load that added nothing new is not visible here.

panels.title: Latest data-quality run

targets.rawSql: SELECT (SELECT max(check_time) FROM data_quality_history) AS "t"

panels.description: check_time of the newest data_quality_history rows (written by the Airflow data_quality_checks task).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'error') AS "errors",
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'warn') AS "warnings",
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'info') AS "info"
         FROM data_quality_history WHERE check_time = (SELECT max(check_time) FROM data_quality_history)

panels.title: aircraft_states end offset

targets.rawSql: SELECT kafka_end_offset AS "end offset" FROM (SELECT * FROM pipeline_monitor_samples ORDER BY sampled_at DESC LIMIT 1) s

panels.description: Sum of the partitions' high watermarks = messages ever written to the topic. N/A when the broker could not be asked.

panels.title: Messages retained

targets.rawSql: SELECT kafka_end_offset - kafka_start_offset AS "retained" FROM (SELECT * FROM pipeline_monitor_samples ORDER BY sampled_at DESC LIMIT 1) s

panels.description: High minus low watermark: messages still on the broker (the low watermark moves when retention deletes old segments).

panels.title: Messages produced per minute (aircraft_states)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sampled_at AS time,
       GREATEST(kafka_end_offset - lag(kafka_end_offset) OVER w, 0) * 60.0
         / NULLIF(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM sampled_at - lag(sampled_at) OVER w), 0) AS "messages per minute"
FROM pipeline_monitor_samples
WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at) AND kafka_ok
WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY sampled_at)
ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Rate derived from the change of the end offset between monitor samples. Only changed aircraft states are published.

panels.title: Last batch committed (min ago)

targets.rawSql: SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - spark_committed_at) / 60.0 AS "minutes" FROM (SELECT * FROM pipeline_monitor_samples ORDER BY sampled_at DESC LIMIT 1) s

panels.description: mtime of the newest commits/<batch> file in the live checkpoint (read-only). Spark commits a batch only when new Kafka data arrived, so a long gap is only a problem if ingestion is still writing (see Component status).

panels.title: Kafka → Spark lag (messages)

targets.rawSql: SELECT spark_lag AS "lag" FROM (SELECT * FROM pipeline_monitor_samples ORDER BY sampled_at DESC LIMIT 1) s

panels.description: Kafka end offset minus the end offsets of the last committed Spark batch (from the checkpoint). 0 = caught up. N/A whenever it cannot be computed reliably (broker down, partition mismatch, checkpoint ahead of the topic).

panels.title: Kafka → Spark lag over time

targets.rawSql: SELECT sampled_at AS time, spark_lag AS "lag (messages)" FROM pipeline_monitor_samples WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at) ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Gaps = lag could not be computed at that sample.

panels.title: Output activity (last 15 min)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sampled_at AS time, spark_batches_15m AS "Spark batches committed", ingestion_files_15m AS "Ingestion Parquet files"
          FROM pipeline_monitor_samples WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at) ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Rolling 15-minute counts at each sample. Spark: commit files retained in the checkpoint (Spark keeps about the last 100 batches). Ingestion: Parquet files in the newest date partition of data/processed.

panels.title: Latest DAG run

targets.rawSql: SELECT upper(state) AS "state" FROM (SELECT * FROM pipeline_airflow_runs WHERE dag_id = 'opensky_pipeline' ORDER BY COALESCE(started_at, queued_at) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) r

panels.description: State of the newest opensky_pipeline run, copied from Airflow's metadata DB by the monitor.

targets.rawSql: SELECT max(ended_at) AS "t" FROM pipeline_airflow_runs WHERE dag_id = 'opensky_pipeline' AND state = 'success'

panels.title: Failed task instances (24 h)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "failed" FROM pipeline_airflow_runs r, jsonb_each_text(r.task_states) t
        WHERE r.dag_id = 'opensky_pipeline' AND COALESCE(r.started_at, r.queued_at) > now() - interval '24 hours'
          AND t.value = 'failed'

panels.description: Tasks whose final state is 'failed' in opensky_pipeline runs started in the last 24 hours (upstream_failed not counted).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'failed') AS "failed", count(*) AS "total" FROM pipeline_airflow_runs
        WHERE dag_id = 'opensky_pipeline' AND COALESCE(started_at, queued_at) > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: Recent DAG runs (both DAGs, newest first)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.dag_id AS "dag", r.run_type AS "type", upper(r.state) AS "state",
       COALESCE(r.started_at, r.queued_at) AS "started",
       round((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM COALESCE(r.ended_at, now()) - COALESCE(r.started_at, r.queued_at)) / 60.0)::numeric, 1) AS "minutes",
       (SELECT string_agg(t.key, ', ' ORDER BY t.key) FROM jsonb_each_text(r.task_states) t WHERE t.value = 'failed') AS "failed tasks"
FROM pipeline_airflow_runs r
ORDER BY COALESCE(r.started_at, r.queued_at) DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 15

panels.description: Up to 24 runs per DAG are kept in pipeline_airflow_runs. 'minutes' of an unfinished run = time since it started/queued.

panels.title: Total observations

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "observations" FROM aircraft_observations

panels.description: Exact count(*) of aircraft_observations on every refresh; fine for millions of rows, switch to pg_class.reltuples if it ever gets slow.

panels.title: Airborne (newest 15-min window)

targets.rawSql: SELECT aircraft AS "airborne" FROM v_current_status WHERE flight_status = 'AIRBORNE'

panels.description: From the existing view v_current_status: latest observation per aircraft within 15 minutes of the newest observation.

targets.rawSql: SELECT aircraft AS "on ground" FROM v_current_status WHERE flight_status = 'ON_GROUND'
SELECT pg_database_size(current_database()) AS "size"

panels.title: aircraft_observations size

targets.rawSql: SELECT pg_total_relation_size('aircraft_observations') AS "size"

panels.description: Table plus its indexes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT numbackends AS "connections" FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database()

panels.title: Observations loaded by hour (observation time)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('hour', observation_time) AS time,
                 count(*) FILTER (WHERE flight_status = 'AIRBORNE') AS "airborne",
                 count(*) FILTER (WHERE flight_status = 'ON_GROUND') AS "on ground"
          FROM aircraft_observations WHERE $__timeFilter(observation_time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Rows in PostgreSQL per hour of observation_time. Empty when the selected range holds no loaded data (stale pipeline).

panels.title: Data-quality findings per Airflow run

targets.rawSql:
SELECT check_time AS time,
                 count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'error') AS "errors",
                 count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'warn') AS "warnings",
                 count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'info') AS "info"
          FROM data_quality_history WHERE $__timeFilter(check_time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Number of data-quality checks per status in each run of data_quality_history (15 checks per run).

panels.title: Issues by severity

targets.rawSql:
SELECT severity, count(*) AS "checks", count(*) FILTER (WHERE status <> 'ok') AS "with findings",
                 sum(issue_count)::bigint AS "issue rows"
          FROM data_quality_history WHERE check_time = (SELECT max(check_time) FROM data_quality_history)
          GROUP BY severity ORDER BY CASE severity WHEN 'error' THEN 1 WHEN 'warn' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

panels.description: severity = what the check is allowed to report (error / warn / info); issue rows = sum of issue_count.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT check_name AS "check", severity, status, issue_count AS "issues", rows_checked AS "rows checked",
                 round((100.0 * issue_count / NULLIF(rows_checked, 0))::numeric, 3) AS "issue %", detail
          FROM data_quality_history WHERE check_time = (SELECT max(check_time) FROM data_quality_history) AND status <> 'ok'
          ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'error' THEN 1 WHEN 'warn' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, issue_count DESC

options.content:
**Collected, and from where**
- *PostgreSQL panels*: existing tables/views (`aircraft_observations`, `v_current_status`, `data_quality_history`) read live with a read-only role.
- *Kafka, Spark, ingestion, Airflow panels*: one sample per minute written by the `monitor` service to `pipeline_monitor_samples` / `pipeline_airflow_runs`
  (Kafka watermarks from the broker, Spark time and offsets from the live checkpoint, newest Parquet file, Airflow's metadata DB - all read-only).

**Not available (and why)**
- Container up/down, CPU, memory and restart counts: would need the Docker socket or cAdvisor; neither is added. Service health above is *inferred from activity*.
- Kafka consumer-group lag: Spark does not commit offsets to Kafka, so lag is computed from the checkpoint instead (and left empty when that is not reliable).
- Spark internals (input rate, batch duration, state size): Spark exposes them only through its metrics sink / UI, which are not enabled.
- Airflow scheduler heartbeat: not read directly; a scheduler that has stopped shows up as a run that stays QUEUED/RUNNING (STUCK) or no new run.
- The monitor itself is the single source for its panels: if it stops, those panels turn UNKNOWN/DOWN rather than keep showing old values.
